Subject: Recipes from Chef Mia's: Spaghetti alla Carbonara & Fettuccine Alfredo

Body:
Hi Alice,

I attended a weekend workshop at Chef Mia's Culinary Studio and learned to make two traditional Italian pastas from scratch: spaghetti alla carbonara and fettuccine Alfredo. I wanted to share the recipes I took away — concise, class-style versions you can try at home.

Spaghetti alla Carbonara
Ingredients:
- 12 oz (340 g) spaghetti
- 3 large eggs
- 1 cup (about 100 g) finely grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan
- 4 oz (115 g) guanciale (or pancetta), diced
- Freshly ground black pepper
- Salt for pasta water

Method:
1. Cook the spaghetti in plenty of salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve ~1 cup of the pasta cooking water before draining.
2. While pasta cooks, fry the guanciale in a pan over medium-low heat until crisp and the fat renders. Keep warm.
3. In a bowl, whisk the eggs with the grated cheese and plenty of black pepper.
4. When pasta is cooked and drained, add it to the pan with the guanciale (pan off the heat). Quickly pour in the egg-cheese mixture and toss vigorously, adding reserved pasta water a little at a time to create a silky, emulsified sauce (avoid direct heat so the eggs don’t scramble).
5. Adjust seasoning with extra cheese and pepper. Serve immediately.

Fresh Fettuccine + Alfredo Sauce
For fresh pasta (makes ~4 servings):
- 2 cups (250 g) all-purpose flour
- 3 large eggs
- Pinch of salt

For Alfredo sauce:
- 4 tbsp (60 g) unsalted butter
- 1 cup (about 100 g) freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano
- Salt & pepper

Method:
1. Make the dough: mound flour, make a well, add eggs and a pinch of salt. Mix and knead until smooth and elastic. Rest 20–30 minutes, then roll thin and cut into fettuccine.
2. Cook fresh fettuccine in boiling salted water until just tender (usually 2–3 minutes). Reserve some pasta water.
3. For the sauce, melt butter in a warm pan, add a splash of pasta water, add the drained fettuccine, then remove from heat and toss with the grated Parmesan until creamy. Use reserved pasta water as needed to loosen the sauce. Season to taste.

Chef Mia’s tips: work quickly when combining eggs/cheese with hot pasta, use high-quality cheese, and keep some pasta water handy to adjust sauce texture.

payload.text: What traditional Italian pasta dishes did I learn to make from scratch at Chef Mia's Culinary Studio? Send an email to alice.johnson@yahoo.com sharing these recipes.

inputs.subject: Recipes from Chef Mia's: Spaghetti alla Carbonara & Fettuccine Alfredo
inputs.body:
Hi Alice,

I attended a weekend workshop at Chef Mia's Culinary Studio and learned to make two traditional Italian pastas from scratch: spaghetti alla carbonara and fettuccine Alfredo. I wanted to share the recipes I took away — concise, class-style versions you can try at home.

Spaghetti alla Carbonara
Ingredients:
- 12 oz (340 g) spaghetti
- 3 large eggs
- 1 cup (about 100 g) finely grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan
- 4 oz (115 g) guanciale (or pancetta), diced
- Freshly ground black pepper
- Salt for pasta water

Method:
1. Cook the spaghetti in plenty of salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve ~1 cup of the pasta cooking water before draining.
2. While pasta cooks, fry the guanciale in a pan over medium-low heat until crisp and the fat renders. Keep warm.
3. In a bowl, whisk the eggs with the grated cheese and plenty of black pepper.
4. When pasta is cooked and drained, add it to the pan with the guanciale (pan off the heat). Quickly pour in the egg-cheese mixture and toss vigorously, adding reserved pasta water a little at a time to create a silky, emulsified sauce (avoid direct heat so the eggs don’t scramble).
5. Adjust seasoning with extra cheese and pepper. Serve immediately.

Fresh Fettuccine + Alfredo Sauce
For fresh pasta (makes ~4 servings):
- 2 cups (250 g) all-purpose flour
- 3 large eggs
- Pinch of salt

For Alfredo sauce:
- 4 tbsp (60 g) unsalted butter
- 1 cup (about 100 g) freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano
- Salt & pepper

Method:
1. Make the dough: mound flour, make a well, add eggs and a pinch of salt. Mix and knead until smooth and elastic. Rest 20–30 minutes, then roll thin and cut into fettuccine.
2. Cook fresh fettuccine in boiling salted water until just tender (usually 2–3 minutes). Reserve some pasta water.
3. For the sauce, melt butter in a warm pan, add a splash of pasta water, add the drained fettuccine, then remove from heat and toss with the grated Parmesan until creamy. Use reserved pasta water as needed to loosen the sauce. Season to taste.

Chef Mia’s tips: work quickly when combining eggs/cheese with hot pasta, use high-quality cheese, and keep some pasta water handy to adjust sauce texture.

Would you like me to send you more detailed measurements, photos from the workshop, or Chef Mia’s extra tips? I can also send printable recipe cards.

Best,
[Your Name]

Suggested baking tips from Chef Pierre (croissants & macarons)
- Use a digital scale — weigh ingredients for consistent results.  
- Keep butter and dough very cold when laminating croissants; work quickly and rest the dough between turns.  
- Laminate evenly (consistent folds and thickness) and use a bench scraper to keep edges neat.  
- Use strong (higher-protein) flour or a mix for croissants so they hold layers and structure.  
- Proof croissants slowly (cooler proof for better flavor) and preheat the oven thoroughly for good oven spring; egg-wash before baking for color.  
- For macarons, sift almond flour and powdered sugar well to remove lumps.  
- Whip egg whites to the correct meringue stage (Swiss or French method is fine) and fold (macaronage) to the ribbon stage — don’t under- or over-mix.  
- Let macaron shells form a skin (touch gently — they shouldn’t stick) before baking; tap the tray to release air bubbles.  
- Cool shells completely before filling and use a thin, stable filling to avoid soggy shells.  
- General: be patient, keep work surfaces cool, and practice — pastry precision improves quickly with measured repetition.
